The little bookstore on Pine Street opens before the rest of the shops.
I stopped at the bookstore while the rain fell softly outside.
A bell above the bookstore door rang as I stepped inside.
The shelves were crowded with old maps, cookbooks, and tales of the sea.
Sunlight fell across the low shelves beside the front window.
Someone had left a handwritten note beside a stack of used books.
I picked a thin novel and read the first page by the window.
I went home with a book I had never heard of before.
By the time I left, I already knew when I would come back.
We started our walk just after sunrise, when the park was still quiet.
On Sunday morning, we followed the footpath into the park.
We took the long way through the park while the air was still cool.
A dog ran ahead of us, chasing leaves across the empty path.
Ducks crossed the pond in a loose line, leaving small waves behind.
The trees kept the path cool even as the sun climbed higher.
We sat on a wooden bench and watched the park fill up.
We stopped for a while before turning back toward home.
By the end of the walk, the streets around the park were waking up.
On Saturday, I carried an empty bag to the neighborhood market.
The market stalls were already busy when I arrived.
I walked to the market before the morning rush.
A baker had set fresh bread next to jars of dark honey.
There were pears in wooden boxes and flowers in blue buckets.
Two neighbors stood by the fruit stall, talking about the weather.
I bought enough for lunch and walked home along the river.
My bag felt much heavier on the walk home.
Before leaving, I chose three ripe peaches to share at home.
The train left the city just as the sun dropped behind the buildings.
I found a window seat on the evening train and put my bag at my feet.
The evening train pulled away from the platform a few minutes late.
Soon, the view gave way to fields and small houses with red roofs.
At every stop, a few more lights appeared in the windows outside.
For a long stretch, the tracks ran alongside a shallow river.
I watched the view until my stop was announced.
When I stepped off the train, the air smelled like rain.
By the time we arrived, I had forgotten to open my book.
The lemon cake was already in the oven when my sister arrived.
I decided to bake a lemon cake on a quiet afternoon.
A bowl of bright lemons on the kitchen table gave me an idea.
Soon, the sweet smell of lemon reached every room in the house.
While the cake baked, I washed the bowls and cleared the table.
I checked the oven twice before the top turned golden.
We ate the first slices while the cake was still warm.
I saved a slice for breakfast and shared the rest.
Once the cake cooled, I dusted the top with a little sugar.
We reached the beach before the first boats left the harbor.
A strong wind greeted us when we stepped onto the beach.
We walked along the beach while the tide was low.
Small waves broke over the stones and rolled back into the sea.
Gulls stood near the water, looking for food in the wet sand.
A row of footprints curved along the shore and disappeared into the water.
We collected a few shells before heading back up the path.
We stayed until the wind made our hands too cold.
On the way home, we stopped to brush the sand from our shoes.
